SMTO-WEB-0045 — A website asked SMTO to wait before reading it again

GUID: 8a80e7cc-da67-57ac-81b4-4c727f286005
Slug: research-rate-limited
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • The website said it was getting too many requests and asked SMTO to pause, usually for about a minute and never more than an hour. SMTO didn't contact it again yet, and anything it already read is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let SMTO continue; it can use other sources while the website's pause runs. The site will refuse more requests until its waiting time is over.
  2. If you need that exact page, wait at least a few minutes (a site can ask for up to an hour), then send a message asking SMTO to read it again. Once the pause has ended, SMTO is allowed to contact the site again.
  3. Don't ask SMTO to get around the pause by using the browser or a different account. The site asked for a break; ignoring it can get further requests blocked.

What success looks like

  • After the wait, SMTO reads the page, or its answer notes that the site asked it to wait.

If it still fails

  • If the site keeps asking SMTO to wait for a long time, use a different source for that information. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO if it happens on many sites.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • web_research acquisitions.reserve() refused the request because the same URL and tool have an active cooldown recorded from an earlier rate-limited (429) response and its Retry-After value.

What this means

  • The same normalized URL and transport have an active recorded Retry-After cooldown. The rejected acquisition is not dispatched. Earlier acquisitions and their evidence remain; another access needs its ordinary permission and allowance.

Why this can happen

  • The same normalized URL and transport have an active recorded Retry-After cooldown.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained cooldown deadline and transport scope.

How to fix it

  • settle() sets cooldown_until from Retry-After (seconds or HTTP date, clamped to 1-3600 s, 60 s when missing or invalid) after a 429 or rate_limited access_state; reserve() blocks the same scheme/host/path and tool until then. Wait for the deadline before repeating that transport; do not bypass it with Browser, repeated requests or different accounts.
  • Respect the recorded Retry-After before repeating this transport. Do not automatically bypass it with Browser.

Retry and execution caution

  • Respect the recorded Retry-After before repeating this transport. Do not automatically bypass it with Browser.

How to verify the fix

  • Further access respects the recorded deadline and ordinary authorization.

What not to do

  • Do not evade the source cooldown with repeated requests or substitute accounts.

Technical notes

  • The rejected acquisition is not dispatched. Earlier acquisitions and their evidence remain; another access needs its ordinary permission and allowance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
